GEModelR keeps the legacy in-memory engine as the default and offers sparse
execution as an explicit runtime choice. This article runs one small generated
model through both workflows. The fixture is deterministic and contains no
external TABLO or HAR inputs.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
helperPath = if (file.exists("helpers.R")) {
  "helpers.R"
} else {
  file.path("vignettes", "helpers.R")
}
source(helperPath, local = knitr::knit_global())
fixture = makeFirstSimulationFixture()
```

## Run the legacy workflow

Load the same TABLO recipe and input arrays with `engine = "legacy"`, set the
closure and shock, then solve with the matching engine. `postsim = FALSE` keeps
this example focused on the numerical solution.

```{r legacy-solve}
legacyModel = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
legacyModel$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
legacyModel$setClosure("tax")
legacyModel$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "legacy")
legacyModel$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
legacyModel$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "legacy",
  postsim = FALSE
)
```

## Opt in to sparse execution

To use sparse execution, load the data with `engine = "sparse"` and use that
same engine for the solve. The Matrix backend is selected explicitly here.
When changing an existing model to a different engine, load its data again so
the runtime state matches the selected engine.

```{r sparse-solve}
sparseModel = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
sparseModel$loadTablo(fixture$tabloPath)
sparseModel$setClosure("tax")
sparseModel$loadData(fixture$inputData, engine = "sparse")
sparseModel$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
sparseModel$solveModel(
  iter = 1,
  steps = 1,
  engine = "sparse",
  postsim = FALSE,
  backend = "Matrix"
)
```

Both runs use the same three-region model and shock. Inspect their solution
vectors side by side:

```{r compare-solutions}
data.frame(
  region = fixture$regions,
  legacy = unname(legacyModel$solution),
  sparse = unname(sparseModel$solution)
)
```

## Package identity migration

If your code still names the predecessor package, replace `tabloToR` with
`GEModelR` directly. GEModelR does not provide a compatibility shim. The root
`MIGRATION.md` in the source checkout is authoritative for package, option,
environment-variable, and saved-state replacements; this vignette covers only
the legacy-versus-sparse runtime choice.
